title: decade's modules are grouped into server, viewer and shared modules
body:
`src/` holds 28 modules side by side, plus `compositor/` and `viewer/` for their submodules. The non-Linux build compiles only `wire.rs`. It prints that a remote viewer is not built yet and exits. So `main.rs` puts `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` on 27 `mod` lines.

Who uses what, from the `crate::` imports:

- Only the compositor and its submodules use the drawing modules (`text`, `palette`, `draw`, `frame`, `menu`, `panel`, `picker`, `settings`). The one exception is `viewer.rs`, which reads `palette::BACKGROUND`.
- `panes` draws pane bars through `draw`, `palette` and `text`. `draw`, `text` and `frame` take `panes::CellRect`. `picker` takes a `workspace::Workspace`. `menu` lists `apps::App`.
- `workspace` holds a `channel::Router` and a `scratch::Scratch`. `save` and `scratch` read `/proc` through `proc`.
- Only `compositor/viewers.rs` uses `pool`. Only `viewer.rs` uses `hypr`.
- The server and a client (`viewer` or `script`) both use `control`, `files`, `lines`, `gpu` and `wire`.

## Proposal

```text
src/
  main.rs
  wire.rs  control.rs  files.rs  lines.rs  gpu.rs  script.rs
  viewer.rs
  viewer/      clipboard.rs  hypr.rs
  server.rs
  server/
    compositor.rs  rounded.frag
    compositor/  viewers.rs  input.rs  channels.rs  selection.rs  render.rs  pool.rs
    panes.rs  workspace.rs  save.rs
    channel.rs  mcp.rs  scratch.rs  children.rs  apps.rs  proc.rs
    chrome.rs
    chrome/      text.rs  palette.rs  draw.rs  frame.rs  menu.rs  panel.rs  picker.rs  settings.rs
```

`server` holds the modules that only `decade server` runs. `chrome` holds the compositor's drawing and its overlays. `pool` moves under the compositor and `hypr` under the viewer, since each has one user. The modules left at the root are the ones a server and a client share. `server.rs` and `chrome.rs` hold only `mod` lines.

`main.rs` keeps a cfg line on `server`, `viewer` and the five shared Linux modules. That is seven, down from 27. The cfg lines on `main` and the command functions stay.

The moves come first, as `git mv` with only the path fixes they force. A second commit narrows module visibility. After it, `viewer.rs` reading `palette` is the one import into `server` from outside.

## Rejected

- `layout` (`panes`, `workspace`, `save`) and `chrome` as top-level groups. `panes` and the drawing modules import each other, and `workspace` and `save` import `channel`, `scratch` and `proc`. Three top-level groups would import each other in a cycle.
- `palette` at the root. That adds a root module so that the viewer can read one colour.
- A `layout` parent inside `server`. Because `panes` and `chrome` import each other, its items would stay visible to `chrome`, and the parent would make no import private.
- Moving `start`, `stop`, `status` and `list` out of `main.rs` to drop their cfg lines. They print the command line's output. A module holding them would only take a call from `main`.

## Cost

No behaviour changes and no public name changes. Paths in `use` lines change throughout. Foam memories that name `src/compositor.rs` or `src/children.rs` need the new paths.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/913b1d2c
notes.text:
Landed as proposed. `main.rs` went from 33 `#[cfg]` lines to 14: seven on `mod` lines and seven on `main`, `USAGE` and the command functions.

Imports that cross between the root, `server` and `viewer`:

| from | to |
|---|---|
| `viewer.rs` | `server::chrome::palette::BACKGROUND` |
| `server` | `control`, `files`, `lines`, `gpu`, `wire` |
| `viewer` | `control`, `lines`, `wire` |
| `script.rs` | `control`, `gpu`, `wire` |

Inside `server`, `panes` and `chrome` still import each other. `panes` draws pane bars with `chrome::draw`, and `chrome::draw`, `text` and `frame` take `panes::CellRect`.

`proc::tests::under_shell` stays `pub(crate)`. `pub(super)` there would reach only `proc`, and `scratch`'s tests call it.

Open issue bodies that named moved files now carry the new paths. Closed issues keep the old ones.
